review: Reviewed Lin's round-20 request (build and maintain a small weather shelter) and the accepted world-33 develop review (learning 4): a freestanding branch wind screen from 12 qualified branch units (length at least 1.2 m, diameter 1-3 cm), eight paid work rounds, integrity ageing, and a lee-side reduction of only the wind-exposure component by 30% times integrity when wind blows through the screen toward the lee polygon. The review states that if source materials or environmental exposure integration are unavailable, the exact unsupported condition must be reported with no successful construction or protection and no decorative substitute. Inspection found two unsupported physical prerequisites: branch records carry only mass, hardness and flexibility, with no length or diameter, so the recipe cannot be qualified without inventing a branch geometry model; and world wind is a scalar strength with no direction, so lee-side protection cannot be computed without inventing a wind direction. Under this run's operating rule the developer does not author new physical rules, so implemented weather-barrier@1 in scope long-ex14 as a general first release, following the ex13 precedent of an interface that records unresolved geometry. Build with x/y and orientation performs real checks of the 2 m x 1 m footprint and the adjacent 1 m x 1 m lee space (reach, bounds, ordinary soil, solid objects and other people) and counts owned unreserved branch units against the 12 required, then fails with the exact report and both unsupported conditions; nothing is built, reserved or spent. Resume, inspect, repair, cancel and dismantle fail at no cost because no barrier can exist. No exposure, comfort, shelter or reward rule changes. Blocker recorded for the human: a working screen needs separately decided branch geometry and wind direction models. Tests cover the site and branch report, unchanged world state and energy, and failure of every other mode.
